Stephanie —

Appreciate the files. High level these look good. Two clarifying points from our security team:
1) The legend shows an "internal service plane" using a purple shaded border. Can you confirm whether that plane permits east-west traffic between tenant-managed services, or is that plane strictly restricted to control-plane only?
2) For egress destinations the matrix lists "monitoring.ingest.*" domains. We need to know whether those hosts are SaaS (third party) vs Redwood-managed collectors; we prefer explicit FQDNs where possible.

We can take a quick 20-minute call to walk the annotated diagram if that's helpful.

Alex Ramos
Security Architect, Pioneer Health
alex@pioneerhealth.com

Alex —

Short answers here:
- Purple "internal service plane" is control + managed service endpoints (KV caches, scheduler, model-store proxies). East-west between tenant workloads is NOT permitted across that plane; tenant-to-tenant traffic is blocked at the virtual routing layer.
- For monitoring.ingest.* entries: in Hosted we proxy to third-party SaaS partners; in Dedicated and Private we provide an optional Redwood-managed collector (redwood-collector.redwood-inference.internal) that customers may choose to enable. I'll attach an annotated diagram that labels those collectors per deployment type.

Notes about the annotated diagram (attached):
- Callout A: tenant VNICs are mapped to isolated subnets; no cross-tenant routes are created by default.
- Callout B: control-plane endpoints are in a separate AZ-local management network and egress through a separate NAT/routing path; we mark those with hashed borders in the legend.
- Callout C: administrative access (SSH/Jump) is limited to a restricted bastion fleet with KMS-backed session tokens.

I'm attaching "annotated_network_diagram.vsdx" — contains callouts aligned to the legend.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
